Reads the config_entries field of a device registry WebSocket result. The replacements are config_entry_id and config_subentry_id; the old fields 'are kept for backwards compatibility and are deprecated; they are scheduled for removal in Home Assistant Core 2027.8.' Until then the old field is derived from the new one, so nothing is broken today. The WebSocket fields keep this date: the move to 2027.10 announced on 2026-09-15 covers the Python DeviceEntry properties only, and that post states the WebSocket API is unaffected.

'created_at and modified_at are managed by the device registry itself, and passing them to DeviceRegistry.async_get_or_create never had any effect -- the values were ignored. Simply drop the arguments.' Removed in Home Assistant Core 2027.9, so there is no replacement field: delete the argument. Only the DeviceInfo(...) and async_get_or_create(...) call forms are matched; a plain dict literal {"created_at": ...} is not, because nothing in the file proves it is device info.

Simply drop the arguments.' Removed in Home Assistant Core 2027.9, so there is no replacement field: delete the argument. Only the DeviceInfo(...) and async_get_or_create(...) call forms are matched; a plain dict literal {"modified_at": ...} is not, because nothing in the file proves it is device info.

Reads DeviceRegistry.deleted_devices. 'deleted_devices is an internal implementation detail of the device registry, and the whole attribute is now deprecated -- there is no supported public use. Accessing it in any way is deprecated.' Removed in Home Assistant Core 2027.9. There is no replacement: a deleted device is registry bookkeeping, so the read has to go. Reported only where the receiver is proven to be a DeviceRegistry.

Uses DeviceRegistry.devices as a mapping. 'Using it as a mapping -- subscription, .get(), .values(), .keys(), or membership by device id (device_id in registry.devices) -- is deprecated.' Removed in Home Assistant Core 2027.9. Iterating the same attribute still works and is not reported: for device in registry.devices, len(registry.devices) and value membership (device_entry in registry.devices) are the supported uses. For a lookup by id call registry.async_get(device_id), or use async_entries_for_config_entry and the other helpers. Reported only where the receiver is proven to be a DeviceRegistry, so a coordinator's own .devices dict is never flagged.

A custom integration reading it logs a warning from Home Assistant Core 2026.10, and 'the properties remain available to custom integrations until Home Assistant Core 2027.10, two releases later than the 2027.8 given in the earlier post.' Detected only where the receiver is proven to be a device entry, including a deleted or child device (a registry lookup, an annotation, or the async_remove_config_entry_device contract); hass.config_entries is never flagged.
